data.one_liner: A Flutter widget that renders animated metaballs using shaders.
data.what_it_does: Provides a highly configurable metaballs visual effect that animates based on cursor or touch input. It uses shader code for performant rendering on web, mobile, and desktop platforms.
use_when: You need a fluid, animated visual effect for backgrounds or UI embellishments
Cross‑platform projects where performance matters and you want a ready‑made metaballs widget
avoid_when: You require custom physics or non‑visual metaball logic
You need a package that offers extensive interaction handling beyond the provided effects
strengths: Shader‑based rendering gives smooth performance on all platforms
Many configurable parameters (color, gradient, effects, glow, etc.)
Works on web, mobile, and desktop without extra setup
weaknesses: Limited to visual metaball effects, no deeper physics simulation
Documentation focuses on usage; advanced customization may require reading source
data.minimal_example:
Metaballs(
  color: const Color.fromARGB(255, 66, 133, 244),
  effect: MetaballsEffect.follow(growthFactor: 1, smoothing: 1, radius: 0.5),
  gradient: LinearGradient(
    colors: [Color.fromARGB(255, 90, 60, 255), Color.fromARGB(255, 120, 255, 255)],
    begin: Alignment.bottomRight,
    end: Alignment.topLeft,
  ),
  metaballs: 40,
  animationDuration: const Duration(milliseconds: 200),
  speedMultiplier: 1,
  bounceStiffness: 3,
  minBallRadius: 15,
  maxBallRadius: 40,
  glowRadius: 0.7,
  glowIntensity: 0.6,
  child: const Text('METABALLS'),
);
